# Installing Mini-Me

## What you need

- A computer with **Windows 10 or Windows 11**.
- An **internet connection** (the first setup downloads a few things).
- **Administrator rights**, *only during installation and the first setup*: you need to be able
  to open **PowerShell as administrator**. If you can't, ask your IT team to be there.
- An **API key** from an AI company (for example OpenAI, Anthropic or Google). This is like a
  password that lets Mini-Me use that company's AI. Your team lead or IT team can tell you which
  one to use. See [What is an API key?](glossary.qmd#api-key)

## Step 1 — Download the app

1. You will receive Mini-Me as a **.zip file** (a compressed folder), for example
   `mini-me-desktop-v0.3.39-windows-x64.zip`.
2. Save it in your **Downloads** folder (most browsers do this automatically). The install
   command in the next step looks for it there.

## Step 2 — Install it into Program Files {#program-files}

Mini-Me **only works from this folder**:

```
C:\Program Files\mini-me-desktop
```

It won't start properly from Downloads, Documents, the Desktop or anywhere else. Windows doesn't
let you copy files into Program Files the normal way, so we use **PowerShell as administrator**
to put it there. You don't need to unzip the file yourself — the command below does it for you.

### Open PowerShell as administrator

1. Click the **Start** button and type **PowerShell**.
2. **Right-click** *Windows PowerShell* and choose **Run as administrator**.
3. Windows asks *"Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?"* — click
   **Yes**.
4. A blue (or black) window opens. Its title starts with **Administrator:**.

::: {.image-placeholder}
**File:** `images/install-powershell-admin.png`\
**Show:** The Start menu with *PowerShell* searched and the right-click menu showing
*Run as administrator*.
:::
<!-- ![Opening PowerShell as administrator](images/install-powershell-admin.png) -->

### Run the install command

1. **Copy** the command below (click the copy icon in its top-right corner).
2. Click inside the PowerShell window and **right-click** to paste it.
3. Press **Enter**.

```powershell
$zip = Get-ChildItem "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\mini-me-desktop-*-windows-x64.zip" | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
$unzipped = "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\mini-me-desktop-install"
if (Test-Path $unzipped) { Remove-Item $unzipped -Recurse -Force }
Expand-Archive -Path $zip.FullName -DestinationPath $unzipped
if (Test-Path "C:\Program Files\mini-me-desktop") { Remove-Item "C:\Program Files\mini-me-desktop" -Recurse -Force }
Move-Item "$unzipped\mini-me-desktop" "C:\Program Files\"
Remove-Item $unzipped -Recurse -Force
Write-Host "Mini-Me installed from $($zip.Name)"
```

This finds the newest Mini-Me .zip in your **Downloads** folder, unpacks it there, and then
**moves** the app into Program Files. If an older copy of Mini-Me is already in Program Files,
it is replaced. Your conversations, files and settings are **not** stored there, so they are
kept. When it finishes, it prints **Mini-Me installed from …**. You can then close the
PowerShell window.

::: {.callout-note}
The app is **moved** into Program Files rather than unpacked straight into it on purpose. A
moved folder keeps the permissions it had in your Downloads folder, and Mini-Me needs those to
update itself later.
:::

::: {.image-placeholder}
**File:** `images/install-powershell-done.png`\
**Show:** The administrator PowerShell window after running the command, ending with the
*Mini-Me installed from …* line.
:::
<!-- ![The install command finished](images/install-powershell-done.png) -->

::: {.callout-tip title="If you see red text"}
- *"Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Path' because it is null"* — the .zip is not in your
  **Downloads** folder. Move it there and run the command again.
- *"Access is denied"* — PowerShell was not opened **as administrator**. Close it and start
  again from *Open PowerShell as administrator*.
- If Mini-Me was open, close it first and run the command again.
:::

When you're done, the app is here:

```
C:\Program Files\mini-me-desktop\mini-me-desktop-app.exe
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Important"}
- Don't move the `mini-me-desktop` folder, or the `.exe` inside it, anywhere else. Use a
  [shortcut](#tip-make-a-shortcut) instead.
- You can delete the .zip from your Downloads folder afterwards.
:::

## Step 3 — Open the app for the first time {#first-open}

1. Open File Explorer, go to `C:\Program Files\mini-me-desktop` and **double-click** `mini-me-desktop-app.exe`.
2. Windows may show a blue box saying **"Windows protected your PC"**. This is normal: Windows
   shows this for any new program it has not seen before.
3. Click **More info**, then click **Run anyway**.

::: {.image-placeholder}
**File:** `images/install-smartscreen.png`\
**Show:** The blue "Windows protected your PC" box, with the *More info* link and the
*Run anyway* button visible.
:::
<!-- ![Click More info, then Run anyway](images/install-smartscreen.png) -->

The app opens and starts the **Get Started** guide. Continue with
[First-time setup](first-time-setup.qmd).

## Tip — make a shortcut {#tip-make-a-shortcut}

To open Mini-Me more easily next time, make a shortcut on your Desktop. **Don't move or copy
the app itself** out of Program Files.

1. In `C:\Program Files\mini-me-desktop`, right-click `mini-me-desktop-app.exe`.
2. Choose **Show more options → Create shortcut** (on Windows 10, just **Create shortcut**).
3. Windows says it can't create the shortcut there and offers to put it **on the desktop
   instead** — click **Yes**.

You can now open Mini-Me from the shortcut on your Desktop.

## Updating Mini-Me

You don't need to download new versions by hand. When a new version is available, a button
appears at the bottom of the window (for example **Download 0.4.0**). Click it to download the
update, then click
**Restart to Update**. Your conversations and files are kept.

::: {.image-placeholder}
**File:** `images/install-update-button.png`\
**Show:** The bottom bar of the app with the update / *Restart to Update* button.
:::
<!-- ![The update button in the bottom bar](images/install-update-button.png) -->
